item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-0e053e8a144aca6c","start_unit":20,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"On August 7, 2023, Bangladesh announced that it would replace the Digital Security Act, which CPJ said had been routinely used to criminalize journalists. The proposed replacement would substitute fines for jail for defamation and provide bail, but many DSA provisions were expected to remain; more than 7,000 cases had been filed under the DSA since 2018, with journalists facing arrest, enforced disappearance, and alleged torture in retaliation for reporting.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; announcement and reported implementation intent, but the source does not establish final enactment or enforcement of the replacement law during the period.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the announcement to the Bangladesh government led by Sheikh Hasina, but does not document her personal order or involvement.","limitations":["CPJ reports allegations and calls for safeguards; it does not establish that the proposed replacement was enacted or that prior abuses were remedied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1e27f0cd1490508d","start_unit":20,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"In 2023, Bangladesh authorities registered and pursued Digital Security Act investigations against journalist Adhora Yeasmean and her source over an investigative report alleging crimes by a religious organization and its leader. CPJ reported that the DSA had frequently been used against critical journalists; it also reported a March 2023 arrest of a Prothom Alo reporter and multiple investigations into the newspaper's leadership and staff. Yeasmean was summoned for questioning, and CPJ called for the investigation to be dropped.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes actions by Bangladesh authorities; it does not prove Sheikh Hasina personally directed these particular investigations.","limitations":["The source records CPJ's account and reviewed documents, but does not report a final judicial outcome or establish personal attribution to Hasina."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9e1afdcfa8764d79","start_unit":20,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"In July 2023, police opened DSA investigations into journalists Nazmus Sakib and Md Emdadul Haque after a newspaper mistakenly used Sheikh Hasina's photograph in an article about Hun Sen's resignation; the newspaper promptly published a correction and apology. The complaint alleged anti-state crimes and conspiratorial news, while Sakib and Haque believed the case was connected to internal press-club elections and opposition to Awami League-aligned journalists. A local government leader also sought cancellation of the newspaper's license, and police used tear gas, rubber bullets, water cannons, beatings, and mass arrests against opposition protesters in late July.","question_ids":["2B.6","3B.1","3B.8","3B.9","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly within July-August 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the investigations and protest response to Bangladesh authorities and reports links to Awami League-aligned actors; it does not establish Hasina's personal instruction.","limitations":["Claims about political motive are reported beliefs and allegations; the source does not provide a final court determination or direct evidence of Hasina's personal involvement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3695a593caa893a2","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh deposited its instrument of ratification for the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons in September 2019.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Pre-period institutional context relevant to the posture inherited in 2023; no 2023 action is documented.","ruler_attribution":"The source records Bangladesh's state action during Sheikh Hasina's premiership but does not identify her personal role.","limitations":["The document does not assess 2023 implementation, funding, compliance, or operational safeguards."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e2c7f1e2300ec5d3","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"The UN Office for Disarmament Affairs lists Bangladesh as a state party that submitted its declaration under Article 2 of the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons on February 21, 2021.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Pre-period institutional context relevant to 2023; no 2023 declaration or implementation activity is documented.","ruler_attribution":"The record concerns Bangladesh as a state during Hasina's premiership; it does not establish her personal involvement.","limitations":["The listing does not provide evidence about 2023 compliance, domestic safeguards, or enforcement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e7b5a928c642cb1c","start_unit":19,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"At an IAEA conference held November 6-10, 2023, a Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority presentation described the government's agreement with Russia to establish two Rooppur nuclear power units and proposed an approximately 11,500 m3 interim disposal facility for very low-level radioactive waste at the plant site.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","5B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The presentation attributes the nuclear project to the Government of Bangladesh; it does not establish Sheikh Hasina's personal decisions or the facility's operational status.","limitations":["The source is a conference abstract and does not verify construction, funding, licensing, inspection, emergency preparedness, or actual waste-management performance."]},{"source_id":"SRC-433a604cf128952e","start_unit":13,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"RSF describes Sheikh Hasina's 2009-2024 government as using censorship, cyberharassment, pressure from military intelligence, judicial harassment, draconian laws, police violence, and ruling-party militia assaults against journalism. It reports that the Digital Security Act and later Cyber Security Act enabled detention and proceedings against journalists, while media outlets practiced self-censorship and state broadcasters lacked editorial independence.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.10","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The account covers Hasina's full 2009-2024 tenure and therefore includes 2023, but is not limited to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"RSF directly attributes the described media restrictions and political context to Sheikh Hasina's government.","limitations":["The page is a current retrospective and does not isolate specific 2023 incidents, orders, or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c499d7b2f1fbcc10","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"A 2024 retrospective alleged that Hasina and family members received six 10-katha plots in a government housing project in 2022, and described broader family property allocations, special security legislation, and concealed or state-secret treatment of some allocations. It further alleged unchecked nepotism, corruption, and benefits to officials and supporters during her period in power.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.5","5B.5","7B.3","7B.4","7B.5","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The reported 2022 allocation and preceding policies are context carried into 2023; the article was published in 2024 and does not document a 2023 event.","ruler_attribution":"The article directly attributes the property allocations, legislation, and alleged patronage to Hasina's governments and family.","limitations":["This is a retrospective opinion-feature article; allegations of illegality, corruption, and concealment are not accompanied here by final court or audit findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-09986e6a994d24c3","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"A 2010 commentary on the Rooppur project stated that Bangladesh and Russia had agreed to cooperate on two 1,000 MW reactors and argued for containment buildings, trained licensed operators, prohibition of reactor experimentation, and adherence to international safety benchmarks. It presented these as proposed or expected safeguards rather than verified 2023 operating conditions.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Pre-period context; the article does not establish conditions in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The article links the project to the government led by Sheikh Hasina but is an external commentary and does not document her personal decisions.","limitations":["The source predates 2023 by many years and is an opinion article; it does not verify later design, licensing, staffing, inspection, or safety performance."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a6eab6eb9c3b813c","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"A 2017 assessment reported that the Hasina government's Rooppur project involved two VVER-1200 reactors, while Bangladesh, as a newcomer to nuclear power, needed a national nuclear-safety infrastructure, an effective independent regulator, competent personnel, and safety culture. It noted limited nuclear-safety manpower and research resources, no safety laboratory at BAEC or the regulatory body, and the need for coordinated policy, education, research, and training.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Pre-period assessment relevant to inherited conditions in 2023; it does not establish whether the identified gaps were corrected by 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the Rooppur decision to the Bangladesh government but presents the safety-capacity assessment as the author's expert assessment.","limitations":["The article was published in 2017 and does not provide 2023 evidence of regulator independence, staffing, laboratories, or implementation."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-c939579cefd0b43a","SRC-262e10205e631f60"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus contains substantial retrospective and pre-2023 material; period fit is identified for each fact.","The documents provide limited direct evidence of Sheikh Hasina's personal orders, formal records, audits, or corrective decisions during 2023.","No supplied document provides material evidence for economic wellbeing, broad social wellbeing, international peace, or most integrity questions beyond the specific property and patronage allegations identified above."]}
